name: Pastoral Scripture
description: A scripture-anchored pastoral Formula with two explicit modes: a concise daily reflection that teaches one takeaway, and expository teaching that moves from observation through interpretation to application.
audience: Christians who want a 3-7 minute scripture-grounded reflection alongside their morning coffee or before bed. Christians who want short doctrinally-anchored teaching — believers refreshing their walk, seekers exploring the faith.
tagline: A passage. Its meaning. A faithful response.
perspective_policy: Pastoral teacher voice, speaking respectfully and plainly to the listener.

narrative_quality_contract.opening_policy: Open with the passage, its human situation, or a sincere pastoral concern.
forbidden_patterns: God wants you to hear this
required_habits: Avoid coercive fear or prosperity claims.
narrative_quality_contract.closing_policy: End with a grounded reflection or blessing.

narrative_rules: Daily reflection mode — Opening word target: 90 words.
Daily reflection mode — Opening beat scripture_reading: read the passage aloud first, unhurried, before any greeting.
Daily reflection mode — Opening beat welcome: a short warm greeting and your name — a few words, not a paragraph.
Daily reflection mode — Opening beat what_youll_learn: name the one thought from this passage the reflection carries.
Daily reflection mode — Opening beat transition: hand over to the reflection gently.
Expository teaching mode — Opening word target: 110 words.
Expository teaching mode — Opening beat scripture_reading: read the passage aloud first, then let it sit for a beat.
Expository teaching mode — Opening beat welcome: greet warmly and give your name; pastoral, with teaching authority.
Expository teaching mode — Opening beat what_youll_learn: name the question this passage answers for the listener today.
Expository teaching mode — Opening beat episode_roadmap: say the shape: what it meant then, what it means now, what it asks of you.
Expository teaching mode — Opening beat subscribe_cta: one warm line; never a hype call.
Expository teaching mode — Opening beat transition: hand over to the first chapter by returning to the text.
Select exactly one pastoral mode for an episode and keep its teaching movement consistent.
title_rules: Titles MUST anchor on a SPECIFIC scripture passage OR a SPECIFIC pastoral topic. Direct and teaching-oriented — never poetic.
Use ONE of these established shapes (vary the passage / topic across the batch):
- 'A Thought on {Book, chapter and verse}'         (for example, 'A Thought on Psalm 23', 'A Thought on John 14:27')
- 'Today's Verse: {Book, chapter and verse}'        (for example, 'Today's Verse: Philippians 4:6-7')
- 'Why {Book, chapter and verse} Still Matters'     (for example, 'Why Joshua 1:9 Still Matters')
- '{N} Lessons from {Book, chapter and verse}'      (for example, 'Three Lessons from Proverbs 3:5-6')
- 'What {Book / Figure} Teaches Us About X'    (for example, 'What the Beatitudes Teach Us About Quiet Strength', 'What Job Knew About Suffering')
- 'Lessons from {Parable / Figure}'            (for example, 'Lessons from the Prodigal Son')
- 'A Devotion on X'                            (for example, 'A Devotion on Anxiety', 'A Devotion for Tired Mothers')
- 'Trusting When X'                            (for example, 'Trusting When You Can't See the Path')
FORBIDDEN in titles:
- Nature/scenery modifiers ('at Sunset's Edge', 'in the Garden', 'Moonlit Waters')
- Atmospheric adjectives ('A Quiet Devotion', 'A Gentle Thought', 'A Reflective…') — keep it instructional, not poetic
- Allegorical decoration ('Echoes of…', 'Whispers of…', 'Glimmers of…')
- Vague abstractions ('Inner Peace', 'Sacred Moments') without a SPECIFIC passage / topic anchor
REQUIRED: every title points at a concrete scripture reference OR a concrete pastoral teaching subject. The audience comes here to LEARN something from a passage, not to enjoy poetry.
Titles MUST anchor on a SPECIFIC passage or biblical figure. Direct, doctrinally-grounded — never poetic.
Established shapes (vary the passage / figure across the batch):
- 'The {Theme} — {Book Chapter}'              (for example, 'The Cost of Discipleship — Luke 14')
- 'What {Author} Means by '{Quoted Phrase}''  (for example, 'What James Means by 'Faith Without Works'')
- '{N} Truths from {Book Chapter}'             (for example, 'Three Truths from Romans 8')
- '{Figure / Book} on {Topic}'                 (for example, 'Paul on Suffering', 'Job on Loss')
- 'Why {Theme} Matters Now — {Book Chapter}'   (for example, 'Why Hope Matters Now — Hebrews 6')
FORBIDDEN: vague abstractions without a passage anchor, atmospheric adjectives ('A Reflective Sermon…'), motivational-style framing.
Every title must point at a CONCRETE passage, figure, or doctrinal subject. No 'inspiring' / 'powerful' adjectives without a textual anchor.

pacing_arc: Daily reflection mode: passage spoken aloud → two or three brief reflections → one practical takeaway.
Expository teaching mode: passage spoken aloud → observation → first-audience interpretation → present application.
Both modes: close with pastoral warmth and no hype.
additional_rules: Daily reflection mode uses about 125 words per minute and stays concise.
Expository teaching mode uses about 145 words per minute and gives interpretation room.

Anchor every devotional in ONE specific passage. Open with the verse spoken aloud, unpack it in 2-3 short reflections, end with a single takeaway the listener can carry through the day. Avoid theological tangents; stay practical and pastoral.

Open with the passage spoken aloud. Move through: observation (what does the text say) → interpretation (what did it mean to its first audience) → application (what does it ask of us). Cite real biblical names and contexts. Avoid pop-culture analogies unless they're genuinely illuminating.
End with a single, clear takeaway the listener can carry through their day — practical, not abstract.
Close on the application — what the text asks of the listener now — with pastoral warmth, not a hype call.

example_topics: What the Beatitudes Teach Us About Quiet Strength
Trusting When You Can't See the Path
What James Means by 'Faith Without Works'
Why Jesus Wept at Lazarus's Tomb
The Sermon on the Mount — Reframed
What 'Pick Up Your Cross' Really Means
Why Paul Said 'To Live Is Christ'
What It Means to 'Walk by Faith'

narrator_styles.label: Warm teacher
narrator_styles.description: Pastoral and clear, like a trusted small-group leader opening the text with you.

narrator_styles.label: Reflective and quiet
narrator_styles.description: Contemplative, unhurried — gives each reflection room to settle.

narrator_styles.label: Grounded and studied
narrator_styles.description: Steady, rooted, quietly confident in the text. Teaching without lecturing.

narrator_styles.label: Pastoral authority
narrator_styles.description: Warm but with teaching weight — a trusted shepherd opening the Word.

narrator_styles.label: Expository and steady
narrator_styles.description: Measured, text-first, verse-by-verse clarity. Lets the passage lead.

narrator_styles.label: Earnest and convicting
narrator_styles.description: Sober and direct, calling the listener to respond — tender with the truth.
